overview: The Jin dynasty briefly reunified China after the Three Kingdoms, but internal weakness and non-Chinese uprisings led to the loss of the north. The Eastern Jin survived in the south as a center of Chinese culture.

items.text: Wang Xizhi creates masterpieces of calligraphy, establishing standards for later generations.
Landscape painting begins to emerge as an independent art form.
Buddhism flourishes with major translation projects and monastic communities.
The Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove exemplify literati withdrawal and philosophical debate.
Eastern Jin preserved Chinese high culture in the south while the north underwent ethnic mixing.

fall.text: The last Eastern Jin emperor abdicated to Liu Yu, a powerful general who founded the Liu Song dynasty.
